alice_support: Heads up — customer_jane seeing rerank flow fail when they switched to client-side batching (batch size 8). Two request IDs: rc-9f1b2, rc-9f1b3. Error returned: 'vector length mismatch: expected 1536 got 1535'. No other obvious error in client logs. Any quick triage?

ben_sre: Can you paste the exact curl or the raw request body? also what time window did this happen in?

alice_support: Pasting the curl they shared (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' 
  --data-binary @batch_payload.gz
```
and the (uncompressed) body looks like:
```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-1536-v1",
  "input": [ [0.12, 0.03, ..., 0.0], /* 8 vectors expected */ ]
}
```
They said they gzip the JSON in the client before POSTing.

carlos_ml: Hypothesis: one vector got truncated during base64/gzip roundtrip or a JS TypedArray/Buffer conversion dropped a float. Also possible off-by-one when flattening arrays for rerank input. Ask them for raw uncompressed body and the exact SDK version.

customer_jane: Adding more context — we uploaded the gzipped file to our temp bucket (s3://acme-dumps/rc-9f1b3.gz) and included both request ids. Billing showed a transient 402 earlier but that was resolved; the error we see in the payload is the 400 vector length mismatch. We can provide the raw JSON if you need it.

ben_sre: Ok. For reproducible triage I need: the raw uncompressed request body for rc-9f1b3, the exact Content-Encoding header used, client SDK version or code snippet that gzips/serializes, and the time window. Please run this helper (we can run on their behalf if they prefer):
```bash
/support-debug --req rc-9f1b2 --req rc-9f1b3 --since 2026-03-16T10:00Z --until 2026-03-16T10:20Z --include headers,raw_body --out dbg-rc-9f1b2-rc-9f1b3.tar.gz
```
Upload the tarball to that s3 path or attach to the ticket.

dina_engineer: Quick local repro I tried: in Node you can accidentally drop the last float if you treat a Float32Array buffer wrongly. Minimal snippet: 
```js
const a = new Float32Array(1536);
// ... populate ...
const buf = Buffer.from(a.buffer);
console.log(buf.length / 4); // should be 1536
// if you slice the buffer incorrectly you can end up with 1535 floats
```
So check any Buffer.slice / subarray calls. Also some gzip libs will silently change Content-Length if you stream incorrectly.

alice_support: @customer_jane can you attach the uncompressed JSON for rc-9f1b3 and confirm whether you're using our JS SDK or rolling your own gzip step? If it's the SDK, include the version.

deploybot: ingest:debug-bundle created id dbg-20260316-871, uploaded to s3://redwood-support-debug/dbg-20260316-871.tar.gz — correlated requests: rc-9f1b2, rc-9f1b3.

ben_sre: Pulled the bundle, grabbed the backend inflator and embedding path logs. One interesting line for rc-9f1b3:
```
ERROR [ingest-worker] request=rc-9f1b3 content-encoding=gzip content-length=4123 inflated-bytes=4096 accepted-bytes=4096 vector-count=8 expected-dim=1536 got-dim=1535
```
So the backend inflated to 4096 bytes (which corresponds to 1024 floats) but expected 1536 floats — looks like the inflator lost part of the payload or the client sent an incomplete gzip. There's also a Content-Length header mismatch logged a few ms earlier.

carlos_ml: Action plan: 1) ask customer to resend the failing batch uncompressed (plain application/json) for rc-9f1b3 so we can run deterministic replay; 2) if replay fails, we add extra validation on our side to return clearer errors + a pre-check for inflated size vs expected; 3) SDK team: add a client-side guard that validates typed array length before gzip and logs helpful message.

alice_support: Summary / next steps: 
- @customer_jane: please upload the uncompressed JSON for rc-9f1b3 and include your gzip/serialization snippet.
- @dina_engineer: can you draft a quick SDK pre-check (TypedArray length -> expected dim) and a small unit test?
- @ben_sre: keep the debug bundle attached to the ticket and note the Content-Length mismatch in your notes.

customer_jane: Will send the uncompressed file in 10m. Appreciate the fast triage. :raised_hands:

ben_sre: Thanks all — I'll follow up here once we confirm the replay. If replay reproduces, we'll schedule a patch for a clearer 400 + SDK check.
